content: A portmanteau inhibitor is a pharmacological agent that combines two distinct drug molecules, each of which functions as an inhibitor targeting specific biological processes. The term portmanteau inhibitor was introduced in 2007 by researchers at the University of Minnesota. These researchers successfully designed and synthesized a compound that simultaneously acts as an HIV Reverse Transcriptase inhibitor and an Integrase inhibitor, thereby targeting two critical enzymes involved in the replication cycle of the HIV virus.
